coverage.note: A chunked body with no Content-Length is counted and rejected. test_no_limit_allows_any_body covers the unlimited case.
After the response has started, receive() returns http.disconnect and no second response or later body is sent. The 413 text and content type are asserted in test_body_over_limit.
The raw receive is called zero times and the response is 413. test_understated_content_length_is_enforced covers the understated header.

The application, router, mount and route limits are each enforced and the default is unlimited, in test_application_limit, test_router_limit, test_mount_limit, test_route_limit and test_default_is_unlimited.
Route, mount and router limits both raise and lower the outer limit. test_application_limit_applies_before_routing covers the application limit applying before routing.

The temp file is closed when the limit is crossed. The multipart framing overhead is covered by test_multipart_overhead_counts_toward_limit, and the generic interruption by test_multipart_closes_tempfile_on_any_interruption.

findings.text: The Content-Length fail-fast is lazy: it runs on the first receive() or the response start, not when the request arrives. An app that does side effects before reading or responding is not stopped early. This is a deliberate trade-off to let inner limits override the outer one, but it is not documented.

No test combines max_body_size with user middleware that wraps receive (for example BaseHTTPMiddleware), or checks websocket scopes through Starlette(max_body_size=...). Middleware-level pass-through for a non-http scope is tested.
collect_http returns a tuple whose second element is always None and is never used, so it can return just the sent list.

summary: All behaviour criteria are met and each has a test that would fail if it broke. I found no weakened existing tests. The findings are advisory only.
